extensions.themeNote: The dark theme is the bare :root default and is therefore canonical; every colorMeta entry carries its light-theme counterpart under `light`. Themes are three-state: system (no attribute), :root[data-theme="light"], :root[data-theme="dark"], each defining the full palette so the manual toggle wins in both directions.

cobalt.purpose: The one live thing on screen: run button, streaming caret, wordmark, links, model nodes, focus ring.

cobalt-veil.purpose: Cobalt at 20% alpha; the spinner's unlit track only.

on-cobalt.purpose: Text on a cobalt fill. Measures 7.53:1 dark, 5.19:1 light.

signal-ok.purpose: Tool execution and healthy state: tool node borders and bars, live instance chip, own messages in a room.

danger.purpose: Failure only. Error text, failed node border and cross mark, the Stop button. Never a warning or emphasis.

on-danger.purpose: Text on a danger fill. Measures 7.80:1 dark, 5.35:1 light.

ink.purpose: The page ground. Tonal step 0 of 3.

surface.purpose: Controls and inset fields: buttons, chips, inputs, graph nodes. Tonal step 1 of 3.

surface-raised.purpose: Content nested inside a container: code block body, detail panel, room log, the 'you' line. Tonal step 2 of 3.

hairline.purpose: Borders on interactive things. The brighter of the two border weights.

rule.purpose: Borders that only divide: card edges, section tops, dashed separators. Dimmer than Hairline so structure recedes behind controls.

text-muted.purpose: Everything secondary: metrics, timestamps, labels, placeholders, empty states. Measures 6.50:1 dark, 6.00:1 light.

title.purpose: The clanker wordmark, in cobalt. The only title on the page.

body.purpose: Primary button labels and fallback prose. The narrowest role in the system.

code.purpose: The answer stream and the task textarea. Same size as Body so a typed task and its answer sit at one optical weight.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked section headings and field labels: TASK, RUNS, CHAT, RECORDED RUN.

meta.purpose: Every reading and secondary string: token counts, durations, costs, timestamps, node metrics.

extensions.shadowNote: Deliberately empty. The system contains no box-shadow. Depth is tonal layering (ink → surface → surface-raised) plus two border weights (hairline for interactive, rule for dividing). See the Flat-Forever Rule.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: Tool-running spinner. Under reduced motion the spinner is hidden and a 'running…' label shows instead.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: Empty answer awaiting its first token. Under reduced motion it settles to opacity 0.6.

motion.name: caret
motion.purpose: Marks a live stream at the end of the answer. Under reduced motion it settles to opacity 0.6.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button :active feedback. Suppressed under reduced motion.

motion.name: skip-reveal
motion.purpose: Skip links travelling from off-screen to top: 0.75rem on focus. Suppressed under reduced motion.

motion.name: scroll-behavior
motion.purpose: JS-initiated scrollIntoView. Chosen at call time from matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'), since CSS media queries cannot reach a scrollIntoView argument.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: The only breakpoint. Below it: main padding tightens to 1rem, the status definition list collapses to one column, toolbar buttons go full width.

container.purpose: Single centred column; no full-bleed sections and no hero.

components.description: The one action per view. Sans-serif label on a cobalt fill.

components.name: Status Chip

components.name: Task Field
components.description: The composer. Monospace at body size so a typed task and its answer sit at one optical weight.

components.name: Transcript Turn
components.description: One exchange: a raised header line prefixed 'you · ', the answer in monospace, a dashed-top footer carrying the run's readings and its actions.

components.name: Run Graph Node
components.description: The signature component. Border colour encodes kind: cobalt model, green tool, text-coloured final. A failed node takes a 2px danger border and a cross prefix. The bar is the node's share of the run's slowest call.
components.css: .ds-node { display: inline-block; width: 152px; padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem; margin-right: 12px; border-radius: 6px; background: #161b22; border: 1px solid #30363d; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; text-align: left; color: inherit; font-weight: normal; cursor: pointer; vertical-align: top; } .ds-node:hover { border-color: #58a6ff; } .ds-node:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #58a6ff; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-node-llm { border-color: #58a6ff; } .ds-node-tool { border-color: #3fb950; } .ds-node-kind { display: flex; font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #9198a1; margin-bottom: 0.1rem; } .ds-node-llm .ds-node-kind { color: #58a6ff; } .ds-node-tool .ds-node-kind { color: #3fb950; } .ds-node-label { display: block; color: #e6edf3; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-node-metrics { display: block; color: #9198a1; font-size: 0.75rem; margin-top: 0.15rem; } .ds-node-bar { display: block; height: 3px; margin-top: 0.3rem; border-radius: 4px; background: #21262d; overflow: hidden; } .ds-node-bar > span { display: block; height: 100%; background: #58a6ff; } .ds-node-tool .ds-node-bar > span { background: #3fb950; }

narrative.overview:
This is the CLI's discipline given a browser's affordances. Monospace is the native hand, not a code-block special case: the heading, the answer, the metrics, the room log and the graph labels are all set in it, because the thing being displayed is machine output and pretending otherwise would be a costume. What the browser adds is click targets, layout, and colour-coded structure — never a different personality. A person moving between `clanker repl` and this page should recognise the same tool, not a friendlier sibling.

Running through it is an instrument-panel streak. Every number on screen is a real reading taken from the run: prompt and completion tokens, wall time, cost to four decimal places, bytes recorded, the duration bar under each graph node scaled against the slowest call. Nothing is rounded into a reassuring summary and nothing is a placeholder. When a value is missing the interface says so rather than showing a plausible zero.

The mood is dense, legible, unhurried. Information sits close together and the surfaces stay flat and quiet so that density never becomes noise; line-height holds at 1.5 throughout and the single accent appears perhaps once per view. Colour is reserved for meaning — kind, state, outcome — so a screen with no colour in it is a screen where nothing needs attention.
keyCharacteristics: Monospace-led, with sans reserved for a handful of control labels
Flat surfaces, layered tonally; no shadows anywhere in the system
Hairline borders as the only structural drawing tool
One accent, used sparingly and always to mark the live or primary thing
Colour encodes kind and outcome, never decoration
Every reading is real; absence is stated, not filled

rules.name: The Kind-Colour Rule
rules.body: Cobalt means a model call. Green means a tool. Red means it failed. This encoding is fixed across the run graph, the transcript's tool lines, and the chat log, and a new surface reuses it rather than choosing fresh colours for the same distinctions.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent. A screen should rarely show more than one cobalt element at a time; if two things are competing for it, one of them is not actually primary.

rules.name: The Two-Border Rule
rules.body: `hairline` outlines what you can touch; `rule` outlines what merely divides. Using the brighter border for a passive divider makes the page look interactive where it isn't.

rules.name: The Monospace-Default Rule
rules.body: New text is monospace unless there is a stated reason otherwise. Sans is the exception, currently limited to primary button labels.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing renders below 0.75rem. Micro-labels that want to be smaller get muted colour instead of a smaller size.

rules.name: The Flat-Forever Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from tone and stroke. A shadow, glow, or blur introduced here would be the only one in the system, and would read as a mistake rather than emphasis.

dos: Do set new text in monospace by default; reach for the sans stack only for a primary action label.
Do reuse the kind encoding — cobalt for model, green for tool, red for failure — instead of picking new colours for the same distinction.
Do express depth with the three tonal steps and the two border weights.
Do give every collection the label → <select> → detail shape that Runs and Chat already share.
Do let anything too wide scroll inside its own container, never the page.
Do state absence plainly — "(nothing recorded for this node)", "No answer was recorded for this turn", "Showing the first 4000 of 9418 bytes".
Do pair every animation with a prefers-reduced-motion alternative that keeps the state change legible.
Do keep interactive targets at 44px and give every focusable element the global cobalt focus ring.
donts: Don't add a shadow, glow, blur, or gradient. The system is flat and has no precedent for any of them.
Don't drift toward a consumer chat app: no message bubbles, avatars, emoji reactions, typing-dots, or gradient send buttons. The transcript is a record, not a messenger thread.
Don't drift toward a SaaS dashboard: no card grids, donut or sparkline chrome, KPI tiles, or empty-state illustrations. Density and real values instead of decorative summary.
Don't introduce a second accent, or spend cobalt on more than one element per view.
Don't render text below 0.75rem; use muted colour for de-emphasis instead.
Don't load a webfont, stylesheet, script, or image from another origin — the served CSP forbids it and the page is expected to work offline.
Don't use a fourth tonal step or a brighter border to solve a nesting problem; restructure instead.
Don't show a rounded or invented number where a real reading is missing.
